title: Rigveda 9.4: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.4: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.4 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 668v-669r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.4.1-10 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 669r
translation.original_text:
1sanā̍ ca soma̱ jeṣi̍ ca̱ pava̍māna̱ mahi̱ śrava̍ḥ | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
2sanā̱ jyoti̱ḥ sanā̱ sva1̱̍r viśvā̍ ca soma̱ saubha̍gā | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
3sanā̱ dakṣa̍m u̱ta kratu̱m apa̍ soma̱ mṛdho̍ jahi | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
4pavī̍tāraḥ punī̱tana̱ soma̱m indrā̍ya̱ pāta̍ve | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
5tvaṁ sūrye̍ na̱ ā bha̍ja̱ tava̱ kratvā̱ tavo̱tibhi̍ḥ | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
6tava̱ kratvā̱ tavo̱tibhi̱r jyok pa̍śyema̱ sūrya̍m | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
7a̱bhy a̍rṣa svāyudha̱ soma̍ dvi̱barha̍saṁ ra̱yim | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
8a̱bhy a1̱̍rṣāna̍pacyuto ra̱yiṁ sa̱matsu̍ sāsa̱hiḥ | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
9tvāṁ ya̱jñair a̍vīvṛdha̱n pava̍māna̱ vidha̍rmaṇi | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
10ra̱yiṁ na̍ś ci̱tram a̱śvina̱m indo̍ vi̱śvāyu̱m ā bha̍ra | athā̍ no̱ vasya̍sas kṛdhi ||
translation.text:
1O Soma flowing on thy way, win thou and conquer high renown; And make us better than we are.
2Win thou the light, win heavenly light, and, Soma, all felicities; And make us better than we are.
3Win skilful strength and mental power. O Soma, drive away our foes; And make us better than we are.
4Ye purifiers, purify Soma for Indra, for his drink: Make thou us better than we are.
5Give us our portion in the Sun through thine own mental power and aids; And make us better than we are.
6Through thine own mental power and aid long may we look upon the Sun; Make thou us better than we are.
7Well-weaponed Soma, pour to usa stream of riches doubly great; And make us better than we are.
8As one victorious unsubdued in battle pour forth wealth to us; And make us better than we are.
9By worship, Pavamâna! men have strengthened thee to prop the Law: Make thou us better than we are.
10O Indu, bring us wealth in steeds, manifold. quickening all life; And make us better than we are.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 669r (numbered 91r by the scribe) (OPenn image 669, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.4.1 ‹-kṛdhi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 669v (numbered 91v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.5.4 ‹barhiḥ prācīnam ojasā pavamānaḥ›. Verses 9.4.1-10 end on this page; 9.4.1 begins on fol. 668v (numbered 90v by the scribe).
